input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer (our party) with a non-compete that runs for 24 months post-term, covers "any product or service that competes with Vendor" in "any territory", and expressly sweeps in acquisitions and internal development. That is walk-away territory under the rule: post-term duration exceeds 12 months and the scope is undefined/unlimited, with no product-specific limitation and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, so it fails the fallback on every material term. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3 (p0044), in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Preferred position applied: delete the restriction; narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, with carve-outs) offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete; it also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which confirms we have made no non-compete or exclusivity commitment. If you need protection for a specific offering, we could discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete binding Customer in Section 12.4.
